chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Karram, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A person takes from the clay of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and benefits from it, while others take and do not benefit from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by the One (God) besides Whom there is no god, no one takes it unless he believes that Allah will benefit him by it, and if he believes, Allah will indeed benefit him by it.'

key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Clay of the grave of Al-Husayn
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: There is no god except Him
key_terms.يَرَى: To believe/consider (in the sense of conviction)

ai.seo_question: Why do some people benefit from the clay of Imam Husayn's grave while others do not?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the benefit derived from the clay of the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is not automatic or physical, but contingent upon the believer's faith (yaqin) that Allah will grant benefit through it. This hadith underscores the Shia theological principle that material objects become effective vessels of divine grace (barakah) only when activated by sincere conviction, distinguishing between the physical substance and the spiritual reality. It highlights the interplay between the tangible relic and the intangible state of the heart, a key concept in Shia devotional practice.
